rows.draftLearningTask: Trace the historical development of medical ethics and apply it to a clinical dilemma.
Explain the purpose of registration and verify a simulated practitioner record.
Compare the functions of the NMC and state councils.
Use the named ethics code and applicable updates to assess misconduct and fee splitting in simulated cases.
Distinguish practitioner privileges, warnings, disciplinary proceedings and removal from the register.
Map duties to patients and society to applicable legal and professional sources.
Use the HIV and AIDS Act to analyze confidentiality, consent and discrimination in a simulated case.
Distinguish civil remedies, compensation and indemnity in a simulated healthcare claim using current sources.
Identify clinical documentation, referral and human-rights considerations in a simulated case.
Prepare a privacy-preserving response to a public or media enquiry.
Distinguish euthanasia, withholding or withdrawing treatment and DNR using applicable guidance and simulated cases.
Use current research guidance to identify consent, oversight and safety concerns.
Explain support and referral needs in simulated assault, sexual violence, attempted suicide, homicide, domestic violence and dowry-related cases.
Analyze barriers in a medico-legal encounter and propose communication and de-escalation strategies.
Identify sources of pressure in medico-legal work and select coping and escalation strategies.
Explain the scope of bioethics using examples from care and research.
Apply autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence and justice to a simulated dilemma.
Compare civil, criminal, contributory, corporate and vicarious concepts and analyze evidence, prevention and potential defences.
Compare types of consent and apply capacity, disclosure, voluntariness, age and emergency considerations.
Distinguish therapeutic privilege, malingering, therapeutic misadventure, secrecy and research participation in separate scenarios.
Distinguish product liability from professional liability and explain the role of indemnity.
Compare Hippocratic, Charaka and Sushruta traditions and describe administration of an oath.
Relate commitments in the modified declaration to a clinical scenario.
Compare rights and duties and distinguish confidentiality from privileged communication.
Assess consent, risk, safeguards and oversight in a simulated clinical trial.
Explain committee composition, review functions and ongoing oversight.
Compare applicable ethical safeguards and oversight for human and animal research.
Demonstrate application of current professional rules in a simulated encounter.
Demonstrate how to design and document a simulated study using applicable ethics guidance.
Classify representative mental disorders including PTSD using clinical features.
Distinguish delusions, hallucinations, illusions, lucid intervals and obsessions using examples.
Distinguish clinical diagnosis from civil capacity and criminal responsibility in simulated cases using applicable standards.
Compare corroborating evidence and limitations when evaluating possible feigned illness.
Explain its relationship to alcohol withdrawal and distinguish it from representative mimics.
Use the Mental Healthcare Act and applicable updates to examine admission, care and discharge in a simulated case.
Select appropriate living or post-mortem samples for representative analyses and explain Locard's exchange principle.
Plan collection, preservation, labelling and transfer and interpret a sample laboratory report.
Explain how to preserve digital evidence while protecting confidentiality and access controls.
Prepare a simulated evidence referral stating tests, preservation rationale and questions for the laboratory.
Prepare a simulated report separating observations, inferences and opinions and document evidence custody.
Compare DNA profiling, facial reconstruction, polygraphy, narcoanalysis, brain mapping and post-mortem imaging by indications and evidentiary limits.
Trace milestones connecting poison detection with clinical and forensic toxicology.
Distinguish clinical and forensic toxicology and explain how dose and exposure influence toxicity.
Classify poisons and relate toxicokinetics and toxicodynamics to investigation in living and deceased persons.
Use applicable statutes including the NDPS Act to analyze a simulated medico-legal exposure.
Plan examination and selection, preservation and transfer of viscera for toxicology.
Recognize representative toxidromes and explain initial diagnostic and management priorities in simulated cases.
Compare representative point-of-care tests and explain false results and need for confirmation.
Explain when supportive care, decontamination, antidotes and enhanced elimination are considered in simulation.
Plan notification, record keeping and specimen custody in a simulated case.
Compare thin-layer, gas and liquid chromatography and atomic absorption spectroscopy by analytical purpose and limitations.
Compare representative inorganic acids, phenol, oxalate and salicylate exposures and justify agent-specific assessment and treatment principles.
Compare presentations and justify agent-specific supportive care, decontamination or targeted therapy when indicated.
Compare arsenic, lead, mercury, copper and iron exposures and explain diagnostic and treatment principles.
Distinguish ethanol, methanol and ethylene glycol toxicity and outline simulated assessment and treatment, including outbreak recognition.
Compare organophosphates, carbamates, organochlorines, pyrethroids, paraquat and phosphides by mechanism and treatment principles.
Compare ammonia, carbon monoxide, cyanide, methyl isocyanate and riot-control agents and justify supportive and specific measures in simulation.
Compare paracetamol, salicylates, antibiotics and representative sedative, antiseizure and psychiatric drug exposures and justify investigation and treatment principles.
Compare opioid, anaesthetic, muscle relaxant, cardiotoxic plant, digitalis and insulin exposures and justify agent-specific management principles.
Compare snake, scorpion, bee, wasp and spider presentations and explain initial assessment and specific treatment principles.
Compare tobacco, cannabis, stimulants, hallucinogens, designer drugs, solvents, mushrooms and food poisoning using representative scenarios.
Link representative industrial and environmental exposures to health effects and medico-legal documentation.
Examine a simulated injured person and prepare a report documenting findings and reasoned opinion.
Demonstrate examination and prepare a medico-legal report in a simulated poisoning case.
Demonstrate examination and collection, preservation and dispatch of relevant exhibits.
Prepare a simulated age-estimation report that states methods, findings and uncertainty.
Review a simulated death and complete the medical cause-of-death certificate.
Conduct supervised or simulated examinations and prepare reports for at least 15 varied causes.
Demonstrate ABO and Rh identification using approved training material and record the findings.
Examine simulated remains and present a supported opinion with limitations.
Identify representative blunt, firearm, thermal and skeletal injuries and write supported medico-legal inferences.
Identify representative weapons and assess compatibility with supplied injury or post-mortem findings.
Identify components of representative bullets and cartridges and explain what they support forensically.
Estimate fetal age from simulated post-mortem findings and report uncertainty.
Demonstrate an authorized simulated examination and prepare an objective medico-legal report.
Demonstrate empathetic consent-based interviewing and examination in simulation, address support for minors and document findings and evidence custody.
Perform a simulated examination and prepare an objective report on suspected intoxication.
Identify representative botanical, chemical and animal specimens and state supported forensic inferences.
Conduct a simulated custody or court-referred examination using applicable NHRC guidance and prepare a report.
Demonstrate recording and certification in a simulated case and document the circumstances and capacity assessment.
Collect, preserve, seal and document simulated exhibits for DNA analysis using the receiving laboratory forms.
Present a simulated expert opinion in court and distinguish findings, conclusions and limitations under questioning.
